verdict.rationale: Shopify's UCP defines a trust-tier system (Token/Signed/Anonymous) where 'stronger identification means higher rate limits and access to more sensitive tools,' and profile negotiation lets the business side compute an intersection of capabilities per agent — a form of built-in, protocol-level rate-limiting and gating. However, this is a global protocol mechanism, not a merchant-facing control panel; there's no evidence of a per-merchant setting to explicitly allow-list, deny, or set custom rate limits for a specific named agent or platform. Missing for 10: merchant-configurable allow/deny lists by agent identity, per-merchant custom rate-limit settings, and any dashboard/API for merchants to manage this beyond the fixed tier system.
